business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Cosmetics and Personal Care Products

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain-China Agreement on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments, signed in 1992 and subject to confirmation of continuing treaty status for the relevant investor

Spain-China Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income, signed in 1990 and applicable subject to residence, beneficial ownership, and treaty entitlement conditions
Spain's applicable network of bilateral double taxation conventions, including the convention with the jurisdiction of tax residence of each shareholder, director, and ultimate beneficial owner
European Union internal-market, establishment, consumer-protection, and customs rules applicable to Spain; no general EU-China free trade agreement is currently in force

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended, particularly Articles 3, 4, 7, 8, 14, 21, 25, and 29; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May approving the implementing regulation of Law 10/2010; Law 10/2010 and its implementing regulation require identification of the natural person or persons who directly or indirectly own or control the entity; Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishes the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales); applicable company-law disclosure and accounting rules include Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Capital Companies Act.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry, notary, or competent corporate authority of the country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board or shareholder resolution approving the Spanish incorporation, investment, appointment of representatives, and execution of powers of attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate shareholder, authenticated by its competent notary or corporate authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special power of attorney for Spanish incorporation and tax-registration formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Ownership chart and ultimate beneficial ownership declaration identifying all natural persons meeting the ownership or control test
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Responsible corporate officer, notary, regulated professional, or competent corporate authority, depending on source jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization where executed abroad and requested by the Spanish notary, bank, or obliged entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of tax residence for treaty, banking, or substance review
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax authority of the relevant residence jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn Spanish translations of foreign-language corporate, identity, ownership, and authorization documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish sworn translator listed by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation, or other legally accepted translator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille normally required for the translator's Spanish sworn translation; source documents remain subject to apostille or consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, banking, and onboarding, screen all shareholders, directors, authorized representatives, UBOs, intermediaries, and major counterparties against United Nations Security Council sanctions, European Union restrictive-measures lists, applicable Spanish domestic sanctions and terrorism-financing lists, and OFAC lists where a United States nexus exists. Conduct PEP, family-member, and close-associate screening under Law 10/2010 and risk-based enhanced due diligence. Verify identity using independent reliable sources, trace the ownership chain to natural persons, document source of wealth and source of funds for elevated-risk parties, screen adverse media, resolve false positives, and repeat screening at onboarding and periodically thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central electronic services portal (Sede Electrónica del Registro Mercantil Central), including the official denominación social name-certificate service at https://www.rmc.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be expressed in an accepted form and must be clearly distinguishable from existing registered or reserved names. Spanish, other official Spanish languages, and permitted foreign-language terms may be used subject to registry assessment. Names may not consist solely of generic or geographic terms, may not create confusion regarding legal form or activity, and may not imply an official relationship or regulated status. Foreign-script or transliterated names should be accompanied by a compliant Spanish registry denomination and must not impair distinguishability or registry processing.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Official state, autonomous-community, provincial, municipal, governmental, royal, or diplomatic designations without authorization
Spain, Spanish, national, European Union, European, royal, crown, kingdom, ministry, embassy, consulate, and comparable official or institutional terms where use could imply public status

Bank, banking, credit, finance, financial, insurance, securities, investment, stock exchange, fund, payment institution, electronic money, and other regulated-financial terms without the relevant authorization or acceptable non-regulated context
Notary, attorney, audit, certified auditor, exchange, guarantee, savings bank, or other protected professional or regulated terms where use could mislead
Terms identical or confusingly similar to existing company names, trademarks, trade names, or well-known institutions
Expressions contrary to law, public order, morality, or public decency
Terms suggesting an activity, qualification, authorization, or official affiliation that the company does not possess
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Submit the name application electronically to the Registro Mercantil Central with up to five proposed names in priority order, the applicant's identification, and the proposed legal form. If rejected, obtain the written registry reason, revise the name to remove identity, protected-term, similarity, or activity concerns, and resubmit. A registrarial decision may generally be challenged through the gubernative appeal mechanism under Articles 324 to 328 of the Spanish Mortgage Law, as applicable, before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública, normally within one month from notification; the filing must identify the challenged decision, legal grounds, evidence, and applicant authority. A judicial challenge may remain available after the administrative route. A negative name certificate is generally valid for three months for execution of the incorporation deed, while the name is reserved in the relevant registry system for the period permitted by applicable registry rules; confirm the operative expiry date on the issued certificate.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office in Spain is mandatory and must be a real address capable of receiving official notices and supporting company records. A virtual office or serviced office may be acceptable for an online cosmetics retailer if the provider supplies a genuine Spanish address, reliable notice forwarding, document access, and, where required, a physical workspace. It is not a substitute for operational substance, inventory, fulfillment, product-compliance records, customer-service capability, or the actual location from which management and commercial activity are conducted. The company must comply with EU Cosmetics Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, distance-selling and consumer rules, product information, responsible-person, safety-file, labeling, and advertising requirements where applicable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official Spain-wide percentage is published for unannounced inspections of newly incorporated online retailers. For a low-risk, non-regulated online cosmetics retailer with complete tax, AML, consumer, and product-compliance records, an indicative pre-operational physical-inspection risk is approximately 5% to 15% during the first 24 months. The risk can materially increase where the registered office is a mailbox-only address, tax filings are inconsistent, import activity is unexplained, product-safety records are absent, cash flows are unusual, or AML, customs, consumer-protection, or regional health authorities identify risk indicators.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), Arts. 20-22, 56-58, 208-216; Real Decreto 1784/1996, Reglamento del Registro Mercantil, Arts. 125-145.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central for name reservation; Registro Mercantil Provincial for registration of the deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura pública de constitución (public incorporation deed) followed by the primera inscripción in the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid in cash at incorporation. Paid-up capital must be evidenced by a bank certificate of deposit issued by a Spanish credit institution; no statutory escrow account is required, but the capital must remain available to the company until registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the public deed of incorporation and articles of association are ratified and the subscription and total payment of the participations are confirmed. (2) The registered office is fixed at [address], Spain. (3) [Name] and [Name] are appointed as joint and several administrators with individual signatory authority. (4) The company’s corporate purpose includes online retail sale of cosmetics and personal care products within ISIC 4791. (5) The administrators are authorized to apply for the NIF, register the company with municipal, tax, and environmental authorities, and execute all ancillary legal filings. (6) All steps taken prior to this resolution are approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificado de Denominación Social (name reservation certificate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central - online application via CIRCE / Registradores portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the request for a negative name certificate with up to three alternative company names. The registry searches the national index and issues a certification if no identical or confusingly similar name exists. The certificate is valid for three months and must be attached to the notarial deed. Notarization is not required at this stage.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application form
Passport or NIE/DNI of each founding member
Three proposed company names in alternative order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because of similarity or registry conflict, resubmit with the remaining alternative names; if a third-party opposition is notified, obtain a new name certificate before proceeding to notarial execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open company-in-formation capital deposit bank account and obtain bank certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution authorized by Banco de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a bank account in the name of the future limited liability company and deposit the minimum capital of EUR 3,000. Request the bank certificate for capital deposit identifying the company in formation, the account number, and the exact balance. This certificate is indispensable for the Spanish notary to execute the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Approved name reservation certificate
Identity documents and NIE of all capital contributors
Bank KYC forms with beneficial ownership statement
Declaration of origin of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises anti-money-laundering or KYC queries, supply source-of-funds documentation and tax-residence certificates; if a formal refusal is issued, open the account with another authorized credit institution and obtain a fresh deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute public incorporation deed before a Spanish notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (Notaría) in the place of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding members or their legal representatives must appear before the notary. Verify the name certificate, capital deposit certificate, and statutory provisions. The deed must include the articles of association, capital subscriptions, administration structure, and registered office. After execution the notary facilitates tax settlement and issuance of the provisional NIF request.
required_dossiers: Certificado de denominación social
Certificado bancario de depósito
Draft articles of association (Estatutos sociales)
DNI, passport or NIE of all founding members
Power of attorney if a representative signs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses execution because of an unlawful clause or missing document, correct the defect and re-execute the deed; if the notary wrongfully refuses, a professional liability remedy is available under Ley del Notariado.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain provisional NIF and settle corporate formation taxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); autonomous community tax office for Actos Jurídicos Documentados (AJD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Modelo 036 to request the provisional NIF, attaching a copy of the public deed. Pay the AJD stamp duty on the incorporation deed within 30 business days of execution using the applicable regional self-assessment form. The provisional NIF remains valid until the final registration in the Mercantile Registry, after which the definitive NIF must be applied for.
required_dossiers: Authorized copy of the incorporation deed
Modelo 036 signed by the legal representative
Bank deposit certificate if required by the tax office
AJD self-assessment form and payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requires additional documentation, refile within ten business days; if the AJD assessment is incorrect, present the deed to the competent tax office for rectification before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company in the Mercantile Registry and obtain definitive NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office; AEAT for final NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory deadline after execution of the deed, submit the first authorized copy of the deed to the provincial commercial registry. The registrar verifies legal requirements and records the company, conferring legal personality and full capacity. After receiving the registration certificate, file Modelo 036 again to convert the provisional NIF into the definitive NIF.
required_dossiers: First authorized copy of the incorporation deed
Proof of AJD payment
Provisional NIF certificate
Modelo 036 for final NIF
Registry fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues defects against registration, correct the deficiencies within the granted period; if the defect is not cured, appeal the qualification to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete municipal activity declaration, IAE census filing, and applicable environmental compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal town hall (Ayuntamiento); AEAT; autonomous community environmental authority for packaging obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a municipal declaración responsable for economic activity only if an office or warehouse is established. For pure online retail with no premises, register the tax domicile and economic activity census with AEAT using Modelo 036. Register under the applicable IAE epígrafe for online retail. If the company imports or places packaged cosmetics on the market as the producer, register with the national packaging waste registry and comply with extended producer responsibility obligations under Ley 7/2022 and EU packaging rules.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Mercantile Registry inscription
Definitive NIF certificate
Modelo 036 registration with IAE
Municipal declaración responsable if premises are used
Packaging waste registration if the company is an importer or producer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality suspends or queries the activity declaration, submit corrective information within ten business days; an environmental classification decision may be appealed to the competent autonomous community authority within one month.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for online retail under ISIC 4791; if a warehouse or distribution center is established, the competent authority is the local municipal government (Ayuntamiento) and applicable autonomous community industry authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial manufacturing or cosmetics production license is required for the online retail sale of finished cosmetic products. A municipal economic activity declaration (Declaración Responsable de Actividad) may be required only if physical premises such as an office or warehouse are used.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) and the relevant autonomous community environmental authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no full EIA or environmental authorization is triggered by online-only retail of finished cosmetic products. The activity does not meet any Annex I or Annex II threshold under the applicable state or regional EIA legislation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission limits apply because no manufacturing or formulation occurs. For any warehouse, comply with municipal wastewater discharge bylaws, segregated waste collection, and packaging waste obligations under Ley 7/2022 and Real Decreto 1055/2022 if packaged goods are placed on the Spanish market.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For any office or warehouse, obtain a municipal occupancy or use certificate and fire-safety clearance in accordance with the local fire code. Workplace conditions must comply with Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales and Real Decreto 486/1997 on workplace safety. Since only packaged finished goods are handled, no major-accident or ATEX clearance is required unless additional hazardous activities are introduced.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores and the electronic sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must obtain a provisional Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) and then a definitive NIF. The application is generally made to the AEAT using Modelo 036, electronically where required, or through an authorized representative. The submission should include the incorporation deed or draft deed, registered articles, Commercial Registry evidence when available, registered address, corporate purpose, identification of directors and legal representatives, and identification documents for foreign shareholders and representatives, normally including NIE or NIF requirements. The provisional NIF is obtained during incorporation; the definitive NIF must be confirmed after registration with the Commercial Registry and submission of the registered deed and related supporting documents. The company must also register its tax census activities, VAT status, intra-Community operator status where applicable, and applicable withholding obligations. A foreign entity without a Spanish permanent establishment generally applies for a Spanish NIF through Modelo 036 when it has Spanish tax, contractual, VAT, customs, or reporting obligations. VAT registration is not a separate general tax number: the Spanish VAT identification number is the entity's NIF prefixed with ES for intra-Community transactions. Registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) and validation through the VIES system are required for qualifying intra-Community transactions. EORI registration with the AEAT is required for customs imports and exports.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a general United States-style check-the-box election for an SL. A Spanish SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal entity. Available statutory regimes may include tax consolidation for qualifying Spanish tax groups, the special regime for entities under the reduced-size-company rules where conditions are met, and other specific Corporate Income Tax regimes. Tax transparency applies only in specifically defined legal forms or statutory circumstances and is not a general elective classification for an SL. Hybrid mismatch restrictions implement EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive principles and may deny deductions or impose inclusion consequences; they are not elective classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA), Spain's value-added tax system, supplemented by customs duties and, for certain transactions, the EU One Stop Shop (OSS) regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 for Spanish-established businesses conducting taxable economic activities; Spain has no general domestic VAT registration threshold. The EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold applies to qualifying intra-Community distance sales of goods and certain electronically supplied, telecommunications, broadcasting, and electronically supplied services by EU-established suppliers, subject to the OSS rules; it is not a general Spanish VAT-registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not currently impose universal real-time electronic invoice clearance for an ordinary SL engaged in cosmetics e-commerce. The Immediate Supply of Information (Suministro Inmediato de Información or SII) requires near-real-time electronic VAT ledger reporting, generally for entities with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million, VAT groups, and entities that voluntarily opt in. Invoices subject to SII are reported through the AEAT electronic system rather than individually pre-cleared. Business-to-government electronic invoicing is mandatory under applicable public-sector rules and is normally submitted through the FACe platform or the relevant public authority platform. Law 18/2022 creates a business-to-business electronic invoicing framework, but its operational scope and effective dates depend on implementing regulations and the applicable transition periods; an ordinary SL should monitor AEAT and regulatory implementation before assuming a current universal B2B clearance obligation. Electronic invoices must preserve authenticity, integrity, legibility, required invoice data, and auditability. Spain also maintains VERI*FACTU and related anti-tampering requirements for eligible invoicing systems, subject to their applicable implementation timetable and exclusions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from Spain to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT under Spanish VAT Law 37/1992, provided the export is made by the supplier or on the supplier's behalf, or by a qualifying non-established purchaser, and the export is supported by customs evidence within the statutory period. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for exemption where the customer is VAT-identified in another EU Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State, and the supplier maintains valid customer VAT-number and transport evidence. Services supplied to non-Spanish business customers are generally governed by place-of-supply rules. A business-to-business service supplied to a customer established outside Spain is normally outside the scope of Spanish VAT rather than technically zero-rated, subject to exceptions for services connected with Spanish immovable property, events, transport, goods, and other special categories. Consumer distance sales and marketplace transactions require analysis under domestic VAT, OSS, import VAT, and deemed-supplier rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration, generally containing the Movement Reference Number (MRN) and the customs release and exit confirmation
Commercial invoice identifying the Spanish supplier, purchaser or consignee, goods, values, Incoterms, and destination
Packing list and transport documentation, such as bill of lading, air waybill, consignment note, or courier export record
Proof that the goods physically left the European Union, including the electronic exit result or equivalent customs-certified evidence
Evidence of the contractual sale, order, delivery, and payment trail sufficient to link the goods to the export declaration
For intra-Community supplies, the customer's valid EU VAT identification number and independent transport evidence or arrival evidence
VAT books, issued invoices, accounting records, inventory records, and OSS records where the transaction is reported through OSS

Inward remittance certificate is not generally a mandatory Spanish VAT export document, and Spain has no general foreign-exchange repatriation certificate requirement; payment evidence may nevertheless be requested as commercial or audit substantiation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain generally imposes no mandatory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. If an export exemption or other VAT exemption is claimed without sufficient customs, transport, customer, or place-of-supply evidence, the AEAT may reclassify the transaction as Spanish-taxable, assess unpaid VAT, statutory late-payment interest, and applicable tax penalties, and deny or claw back related input-VAT deductions or refunds. Penalties depend on the violated obligation and culpability and may be increased for concealment, repeated non-compliance, or fraudulent conduct; invoice and recordkeeping violations may carry separate penalties. A deliberately fraudulent VAT position can also create joint-and-several liability and, where the statutory criminal threshold and intent requirements are met, tax-crime exposure under the Spanish Criminal Code. Refund claims are subject to verification, audit, interest, and recovery of improperly refunded amounts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain); external-transactions oversight is jointly exercised with the Dirección General de Transacciones Exteriores within the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full capital and current account convertibility as a eurozone member state. Capital movements and payments are liberalised under Articles 63–66 TFEU; no foreign-exchange authorisation is required for ordinary commercial payments, equity injections, dividend remittances, or cross-border loans. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted, subject only to standard dividend withholding tax (19% domestic, potentially treaty-reduced) and statistical foreign-investment declaration obligations. Residual screening applies only in the limited context of EU FDI screening Regulation 2019/452 and Spanish Law 19/2003, which impose notification, not licensing, requirements for certain strategic sectors — not applicable to online cosmetics retail.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation deadline applies to export receivables of a Spanish SL. Export proceeds may be held freely in foreign-currency accounts or converted to EUR at the exporter's discretion. Reporting obligations are purely statistical: balances-of-payments declarations to Banco de España are required for individual transfers exceeding €50,000 or aggregated transactions meeting established thresholds. Cash payments above €10,000 in trade transactions are prohibited under Law 7/2012.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (multi-currency EUR, USD, MXN)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for EU/EEA-authorised e-money institutions and digital banks holding a full PSD2 licence and passporting into Spain (e.g., Airwallex, Currencycloud/ANZ Bank, Revolut Business, Penso Payments, Multitudes) as supplementary treasury and multi-currency settlement rails. Medium-to-low feasibility for offshore EMIs, particularly UK-FCA-authorised firms that lost EU passporting post-Brexit; such firms must operate through a Spanish/EU branch, an authorised agent, or an EU-licensed partner. Legal constraints include: segregation of client funds, registration with Banco de España where e-money issuance occurs in Spain, full AML/CTF compliance under Law 10/2010, and balance-of-payments reporting obligations. For the target rails (Shopify Payments, PayPal), a tier-1 Spanish bank account is the recommended primary settlement account, with EMIs serving as ancillary multi-currency liquidity tools, never as the sole clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for the appointed sole administrator or a duly authorised director at initial account opening with tier-1 Spanish banks. The individual must appear with original NIE/TIE, passport, notarised appointment deed, and the company NIF tax certificate. Remote or video-verified opening is available only for EU-resident directors with pre-existing KYC records with the institution and where all UBOs are already known clients. Non-resident, non-EU UBOs or directors will practically always require an in-branch interview or a notarised and apostilled power of attorney, which several tier-1 banks refuse to accept for transaction-risk reasons. For cross-border DTC cosmetics with third-party payment aggregators, compliance reviewers typically require at least one physical visit of the beneficial owner. Strategic planning assumption: allocate a 4–6 week onboarding window and prepare for an in-person interview in Spain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO chain without source-of-wealth documentation — immediately flagged as high-risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised public deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) with sworn Spanish translation; apostilled UBO declaration; bank reference letters from the shareholder's home bank dated less than 3 months prior; 6–12 months' bank statements for each UBO evidencing legitimate source of funds; tax residence certificates of all UBOs; and a detailed explanation of the initial capital contribution (minimum €3,000 or the zero-capital regime with statutory guarantee).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border e-commerce model with elevated chargeback expectations and payment-aggregator settlements (Shopify Payments/PayPal) — potential card-not-present fraud or money-laundering routing risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI-DSS compliance certificate; historical chargeback ratio below 0.9% or a remediation plan; payment aggregator settlement reconciliation reports for the prior 12 months; customer onboarding KYC log; refund policy documentation; 24-month treasury and cash-flow forecast; Spanish VAT/OSS registration certificate with VAT return filing standing; and a copy of the e-commerce platform seller agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin-capitalisation or disproportionate subscribed capital relative to the business profile — indicator of third-party fund routing or informal shareholding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statement demonstrating that the capital injection originated directly from the non-resident shareholder's own account in the shareholder's name (no third-party payer); registration receipt of the foreign investment declaration from the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores; board resolution approving the capital contribution; detailed business plan with revenue projections; pro-forma invoices for initial inventory purchases from EU and Latin American suppliers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the commercial registry entry (Registro Mercantil), the Spanish tax ID (NIF), and the UBO register filings
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Registro Mercantil certificate of incorporation and current officers; AEAT Censo NIF certificate; Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME) publication evidencing the administrator's appointment; certified copy of the public deed and by-laws with sworn Spanish translation; and a notarised, apostilled power of attorney if any representative acts on behalf of the entity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires a SWIFT MT103 wire from the non-resident shareholder's own account (never from a third party) to the SL's euro-denominated corporate account at a Spanish tier-1 bank. The beneficiary name must exactly match the SL's registered name and NIF; the payment reference must state 'Aportación de capital social / suscripción de participaciones' and the EBOPS/BoP purpose code '521 – Equity capital' (or Spanish code 'PK3 – Contributions to capital'). For non-resident investment in a Spanish SL, a statistical declaration to the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores via Banco de España is mandatory under Law 19/2003 and Royal Decree 664/1999; the declaration is post-transaction for investments below €3,005,000 but must be lodged before disbursement for larger amounts. The bank will typically request the foreign investment declaration reference code at account-opening stage. For EU shareholders, SEPA Credit Transfer may be used, but MT103 with full CF code remains the clearing-compliant standard. Inbound funds must remain in the capital escrow account until the notarial public deed evidencing the capital increase is executed, at which point the bank releases the funds to the operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EU/EEA suppliers and vendors, clearing is executed via SEPA CORE Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) with the underlying VAT invoice referenced. For non-EU suppliers in China, the UK, Latin America, or other third countries, the standard clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 with BoP purpose codes (e.g., '310 – Imports of goods' or '511 – Trade credit'); larger first-time or higher-risk suppliers should be settled via a Commercial Letter of Credit issued on SWIFT MT700 (UCP600) with Incoterms 2020, optionally confirmed by a bank in the supplier's jurisdiction. Standby Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT760) are permissible in open-account arrangements where recurring purchase orders support ongoing supply. Documentary collections (Documents against Payment / Documents against Acceptance) are a lower-cost alternative for mid-value consignments. All outbound settlements must remain traceable to underlying invoices and contracts for balance-of-payments and AML compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD plain-vanilla OTC Forwards (typical tenor up to 12 months for SMEs; requires ISDA Master Agreement or the Spanish Contrato Marco de Operaciones Financieras (CMOF)) — primary instrument for hedging USD-denominated sourcing from Asia and Latin America
EUR/USD FX Swaps — permissible for short-term rolling liquidity management when the SL holds mismatched EUR and USD cash flows
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) — permissible for material, multi-year USD procurement commitments such as large-volume supply agreements
EUR/USD European-style Options (e.g., EUR call / USD put) — permissible strictly for hedging underlying commercial exposure; premium paid from the operational account
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) — technically quotable by Spanish banks but economically unjustified for the fully convertible euro; not recommended as a treasury instrument for this entity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) corresponding to the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved by the shareholders' meeting within six months after financial year-end; deposit must occur within one month after approval. For calendar-year entities: approve by 30 June and deposit by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure (cierre registral) until annual accounts are filed; fines between EUR 1,200 and EUR 60,000; suspension of the company's right to register corporate acts; persistent non-compliance may lead to ex officio dissolution or administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Confirmation and Register Update (Actualización de Titularidad Real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro de Titularidades Reales (Ministry of Justice) / Provincial Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the deposit of annual accounts and, in case of shareholding transfers, within one month after the change in ultimate beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML Law 10/2010 penalties for inaccurate or omitted UBO data, up to EUR 60,000; non-disclosure may also block Mercantile Registry filings and expose directors to personal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria – AEAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days after the six-month period following the tax year-end; calendar-year taxpayers file from 1 July through 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 1% per month capped at 12%, plus late-payment interest after 12 months; failure-to-file penalties from 50% to 150% of assessed tax; unpaid liabilities may trigger asset attachment and enforced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT Summary Return (Declaración-Resumen del IVA, Modelo 390)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 31 January for the preceding calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharges of 1% per month capped at 12%, late-payment interest, and penalties of up to 100% for incorrect or omitted VAT liabilities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is mandatory if, for two consecutive years, the SL meets at least two of the following at year-end: total assets exceeding EUR 2,850,000; net annual turnover exceeding EUR 5,700,000; average workforce exceeding 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory for listed entities, financial institutions, and where ordered by a court or requested by eligible shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Real Decreto 1514/2007, as amended) for individual annual accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU for consolidated financial statements of listed groups only.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must maintain an accurate UBO record under Spanish AML Law 10/2010. Any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be reported to the Registro de Titularidades Reales within one month; the annual deposit of accounts functions as the annual UBO confirmation when no ownership changes have occurred.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 6,000 (if audit is required or voluntarily adopted)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly incorporated entities generally qualify for a 15% rate for the first tax period in which they obtain a positive taxable base and the immediately following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions and anti-abuse rules. Small entities may qualify for additional reduced-rate rules where applicable. The general participation exemption may substantially reduce taxation of qualifying dividends and capital gains from qualifying subsidiaries, ordinarily subject to a 5% participation and one-year holding conditions. Tax losses are subject to utilization limits based principally on turnover: 70% of the pre-loss offset tax base for entities with turnover below EUR 20 million, 50% for turnover from EUR 20 million to below EUR 60 million, and 25% for turnover of EUR 60 million or more, in each case with a EUR 1 million minimum annual offset.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria electronic headquarters using the Spanish electronic certificate, Cl@ve where available, or authorized representative access.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer closing on 31 December, the ordinary filing window is generally 1 to 25 July of the following year, subject to official calendar adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish tax identification number, registered address, tax period start and end dates, legal form, activity classification, and filing type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish entity's NIF and registered-office details. A non-resident shareholder does not replace the Spanish SL's identification information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before corporate income tax based on the statutory financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the Spanish SL's worldwide accounting result. Do not report only Spanish-source revenue or remit accounting profit directly to a foreign parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary differences, including non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, impairment, tax-exempt income, and other statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-parent charges must be supported by contractual evidence, benefit analysis, arm's-length pricing, withholding-tax analysis, and proof of actual receipt by the foreign recipient.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments arising from transactions with associated enterprises and any primary, corresponding, or secondary transfer-pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report controlled purchases, royalties, management services, financing, guarantees, and intercompany inventory transactions consistently with the Local File, Master File, accounting records, and customs documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Available tax loss carryforwards, annual utilization, remaining balance, and applicable utilization limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain a year-by-year schedule evidencing origination, prior use, expiry or availability, ownership-change restrictions, and consistency with filed historical returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after adjustments and loss utilization, followed by the applicable statutory or preferential rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the general 25% rate unless the SL demonstrably qualifies for a statutory reduced rate, such as the newly incorporated entity rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Eligible deductions and credits, including research and development, technological innovation, double-tax relief, donations, employment-related incentives, and other legally available items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits require legally sufficient evidence of foreign tax paid or accrued, income attribution, and compliance with statutory limitation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Payments on account and withholding credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior quarterly payments, Spanish withholding tax, installment payments, and other creditable amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all amounts to Modelo 202, Modelo 111, Modelo 115, Modelo 123, bank evidence, and third-party withholding certificates where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax liability after credits and payments, with payment or refund instructions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A refund claim must be supported by the return, bank-account ownership or authorized collection details, accounting reconciliation, and evidence supporting all material credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Required financial, shareholder, related-party, tax incentive, and reconciliation information accompanying the electronic return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign shareholders, related parties, permanent-establishment issues, cross-border payments, and material transactions accurately and consistently with other Spanish filings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without tax payable generally attracts a fixed penalty of 1% plus an additional 1% for each complete month of delay, capped at 15% after twelve months; after twelve months, default interest may also apply. If the tax authority detects an unpaid liability, the applicable late-payment surcharge is generally 1% plus 1% per complete month for delays of up to twelve months, 15% after twelve months, and default interest thereafter. Failure to file after assessment may generate a penalty generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, subject to aggravating or mitigating factors. Incorrect returns may trigger penalties of 50%, 100%, or 150% of the improperly omitted tax, depending on the classification of the infringement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, Corporate Income Tax payment on account, filed electronically through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly payment windows, ordinarily April, October, and December
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December. Entities with turnover exceeding EUR 6 million are generally subject to the minimum payment and mandatory installment-payment calculation based on current-period accounting results.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish NIF, legal name, tax period, and payment-on-account filing type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL files under its own NIF even where the economic owner, lender, or parent is non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax liability method or current-period accounting-result method, depending on the taxpayer's statutory position.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the legally applicable method and reconcile the calculation to Modelo 200 or interim accounting data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory percentage applied to the relevant tax base and resulting payment on account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not reduce the installment solely because profits are intended for foreign distribution; repatriation does not eliminate Spanish corporate income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount payable, bank debit or payment reference, and electronic submission confirmation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain electronic filing evidence and bank debit confirmation in the Spanish entity's tax records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment generally produces statutory surcharges of 1% plus 1% per complete month up to twelve months, 15% after twelve months, and default interest after twelve months. Failure to submit a required payment-on-account return can also produce formal filing penalties and an assessment of the unpaid installment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% on dividends and other profit distributions to non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. The EU Parent-Subsidiary exemption may eliminate withholding where the statutory conditions are satisfied, commonly including a qualifying EU parent, at least 5% direct or indirect participation or the applicable acquisition-value alternative, a minimum one-year holding or holding commitment, subject-to-tax requirements, and anti-abuse conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Spanish payer should obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the foreign recipient before payment, verify beneficial ownership and treaty entitlement, apply the treaty rate only where documentation and domestic procedural requirements are satisfied, and report the payment and withholding through the relevant Spanish information and withholding returns. If excess tax is withheld, the recipient generally files the applicable Modelo 210 refund claim with the Spanish Tax Agency, attaching the tax-residence certificate, payment evidence, withholding certificate, treaty analysis, and proof of beneficial ownership. A treaty certificate does not cure anti-abuse, conduit, beneficial-ownership, or principal-purpose concerns.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic non-resident income tax is generally 24% on royalties and similar intellectual-property income paid to non-residents outside the EU/EEA, with a 19% rate generally applying to interest and other specified income received by qualifying EU/EEA residents. Treaty rates vary by country and commonly reduce dividend, interest, and royalty withholding to rates such as 0%, 5%, 10%, or 15%, subject to the applicable treaty. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive may provide a full exemption for qualifying associated EU companies, generally requiring a qualifying direct participation of at least 25%, a minimum one-year holding or commitment, qualifying legal forms and tax residence, subject-to-tax conditions, and anti-abuse compliance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The general Spanish documentation regime applies to related-party transactions, subject to statutory exemptions and simplifications. A Local File is generally not required for transactions with the same related person that do not exceed EUR 250,000 at arm's-length value during the tax period, excluding specified categories such as transactions involving real estate, transfers of businesses, or transfers of shares or interests in entities. A simplified Local File may generally be available for groups whose consolidated turnover is below EUR 45 million, subject to exclusions. A Master File is generally required where the Spanish entity belongs to a group required to prepare it, particularly where consolidated group turnover is at least EUR 45 million. Documentation must be available by the statutory corporate income tax filing deadline and retained for the applicable limitation period.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime for ordinary Spanish SLs. Substance is nevertheless material under Spanish anti-abuse rules, the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance framework, controlled foreign company rules, the principal-purpose test, beneficial-ownership standards, interest limitation rules, participation-exemption conditions, and treaty interpretation. The SL should maintain genuine Spanish functions, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or operational infrastructure proportionate to the business, decision-making evidence, inventory and logistics records, Spanish accounting, commercial risk assumption, and arm's-length remuneration. A conduit company, artificial service arrangement, circular financing, or entity lacking decision-making and commercial capacity may lose treaty or domestic tax benefits and may be recharacterized or disregarded for tax purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and deliberate concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing online sales, maintaining undeclared payment accounts, recording fictitious expenses, understating inventory or revenue, fabricating invoices, or deliberately claiming unsupported deductions or tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, plus tax, interest, and collection surcharges. Tax fraud may become criminal where the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 in a tax year. The ordinary criminal penalty is imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded, with aggravated cases carrying higher imprisonment and fine ranges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur civil liability for intentional or negligent breach of duties, tax-responsibility liability where statutory requirements are met, and criminal liability for personally participating in the offense. Courts may impose precautionary asset freezes and other measures. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be ordered in criminal proceedings. The corporate veil is not pierced merely because a company is insolvent or controlled by a foreign shareholder.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: VAT fraud and carousel or missing-trader arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using fictitious EU acquisitions, false import documentation, sham suppliers, circular invoices, undocumented cash sales, or false VAT refund claims in connection with cosmetics or personal-care inventory.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT may be assessed with interest and penalties generally calculated by reference to the unpaid or improperly credited amount, frequently ranging from 50% to 150% for serious or very serious infringements. Criminal tax fraud may apply where the statutory threshold and intent requirements are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, financial controllers, and persons knowingly participating in false invoicing or VAT fraud may face joint civil recovery, administrative liability, criminal prosecution, imprisonment, fines, asset seizure, and disqualification. Customs and tax authorities may also deny input VAT and impose joint-liability measures against knowingly involved recipients.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, artificial substance, or treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Spanish SL solely as a conduit for dividends, royalties, or interest; routing funds through nominee shareholders; claiming treaty relief without beneficial ownership; or maintaining no genuine Spanish commercial activity despite representing that functions are performed in Spain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Tax Agency may apply anti-abuse rules, recharacterize transactions, deny exemptions or treaty relief, impose withholding tax and interest, and assess penalties where inaccurate declarations or fraudulent structures are established. The general anti-abuse framework includes conflict-of-law and sham-transaction doctrines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for tax underpayment caused by deliberate or negligent conduct and may face criminal liability where the arrangement constitutes tax fraud, document fraud, or money laundering. Civil liability, precautionary asset measures, and director disqualification may arise; travel bans require a specific judicial order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing manipulation and undocumented related-party payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Overpricing foreign-parent services, underpricing exports, unsupported royalties, interest above arm's length, guarantee fees without benefit, non-commercial loans, or failure to maintain Local File and Master File documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Tax Agency may make a primary adjustment, impose secondary adjustment consequences, deny deductions, assess withholding tax, and impose documentation-related penalties. Spanish transfer-pricing documentation penalties can include fixed amounts per missing or incorrect data or percentage-based penalties linked to the adjustment, subject to statutory caps and mitigation rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil liability for knowingly approving unsupported transactions and may face tax-responsibility or criminal exposure if the manipulation is part of deliberate tax fraud. Mere failure to achieve an expected margin is not by itself criminal or evidence of director misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, structuring transactions to avoid controls, failing to identify beneficial owners, ignoring sanctions or suspicious-transaction indicators, or using payment processors and bank accounts for undisclosed third-party funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish anti-money-laundering legislation, serious and very serious infringements can result in substantial administrative fines, publication or reprimand, and temporary or permanent restrictions on holding management or professional positions. Money laundering can constitute a criminal offense punishable by imprisonment generally from six months to six years and fines that may reach one to three times the value of the laundered property, with aggravated consequences in specified cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, beneficial owners, and employees may incur individual administrative or criminal liability where they knowingly participate, consent, or negligently permit the conduct. Asset freezing, confiscation, management disqualification, and judicial travel restrictions may apply where ordered; imprisonment is not imposed solely for an ordinary compliance error absent the required culpability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False accounting, commercial-document fraud, and destruction of records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining parallel ledgers, issuing invoices for transactions that did not occur, altering electronic sales records, backdating contracts, destroying accounting evidence, or concealing related-party balances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties may apply in addition to criminal offenses involving false documents, accounting fraud, or concealment of assets. Consequences may include tax assessment, interest, fines, confiscation, criminal imprisonment, and civil compensation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and persons who order or knowingly approve false records may be personally prosecuted and may incur imprisonment, fines, civil restitution, asset seizure, and commercial-management disqualification. Corporate criminal liability may also arise where the offense is committed for the company's benefit by senior managers or because of deficient supervision.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying employees as contractors, paying undeclared commissions, failing to withhold payroll tax, using sham subcontractors, or omitting Social Security contributions for warehouse, customer-service, marketing, or delivery personnel.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences may include back taxes, Social Security assessments, surcharges, administrative fines, loss of incentives, and criminal liability for serious contribution fraud or unlawful employment practices where statutory thresholds and intent requirements are satisfied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly or subsidiarily liable under applicable tax and Social Security rules and may face criminal liability for intentional evasion, coercion, or exploitation. Personal liability is fact-dependent and is not created solely by holding office.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs, product-compliance, and import valuation fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating customs value, misclassifying cosmetic products, using false origin documents, splitting shipments to evade controls, importing products without required safety documentation, or deducting import VAT on false customs declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs debt, import VAT, interest, seizure, forfeiture, and administrative penalties may apply. Serious customs fraud may generate criminal liability under Spanish and EU customs and criminal law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and logistics or procurement personnel may be personally liable where they knowingly direct or facilitate false declarations. Authorities may impose asset measures and prohibit commercial activity in serious cases; imprisonment requires a qualifying criminal offense and judicial conviction.
